name: Bennie Thompson
bio: Bennie Thompson has represented Mississippi's 2nd District since 1993 and is the ranking member of the House Homeland Security Committee, which he chaired in 2007-2011 and 2019-2023. He chaired the House select committee on the January 6 attack from 2021 to 2023. He previously served as mayor of Bolton (1973-1980) and on the Hinds County Board of Supervisors (1980-1993).

platform.point: Backs farm programs and notes he has never voted against a Farm Bill.
Aims to close gaps in medical care across underserved counties in his district.
Presents civil rights advocacy, including his role in the Ayers desegregation case, as a core priority.
Supports reauthorizing the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
Pushes for FEMA reform and accountability in disaster response.
Seeks to ensure veterans receive the services and benefits they earned.

economy.evidence: Voted against the 2001 estate tax repeal and 2002 Bush tax cuts and has an 83% Citizens for Tax Justice rating favoring higher taxes on the wealthy.

welfare.evidence: Supports expanding the Affordable Care Act and voted for SCHIP and Medicare expansions.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: 100% NARAL rating and votes against abortion restrictions; guns: F NRA rating and support for universal background checks.

security.evidence: Longtime Homeland Security Committee leader who has opposed warrantless surveillance and PATRIOT Act extensions.

immigration.evidence: Voted against the 2006 border fence and supports legal status for DREAMers.

foreign.evidence: Voted against restricting UN funding and supports World Bank funding, while opposing permanent normal trade relations with China.

energy.evidence: Voted for renewable energy tax incentives and opposes expanded offshore drilling.

tech.evidence: Voted to establish network neutrality in 2006.

education.evidence: Opposes vouchers and private school subsidies and holds a 100% NEA rating.

faith.evidence: Voted against school prayer aid in 1994 and faith-based tax breaks in 2001; 7% Christian Coalition rating.

notes: Much of the voting evidence is from older sessions of Congress.

name: Ron Eller
bio: Ron Eller is a physician assistant from Raymond, Mississippi, who served 20 years on active military duty and then worked about 20 years in private health care. He has since started manufacturing businesses. He was also the Republican nominee for Mississippi's 2nd District in 2024.

platform.point: Calls for immediate border wall construction and cutting federal funds to sanctuary jurisdictions.
Backs an all-of-the-above energy mix of fossil fuels, nuclear, renewables and new technologies.
Wants concealed-carry permits recognized across all states.
Supports allowing abortion only to save the mother's life and opposes federal funding for abortion providers.
Supports photo ID to vote, paper ballot records and ending same-day registration.
Says individuals may refuse vaccines or treatments and supports Right to Try access.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on free enterprise, limited government and fair taxation.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only to save the mother's life and nationwide concealed carry, balanced by opposition to vaccine mandates.

immigration.evidence: Calls for building the wall now and defunding sanctuary jurisdictions.

energy.evidence: Supports an all-of-the-above approach including fossil fuels rather than limiting sources.

faith.evidence: Says religious values should stay central to education and governance.

notes: Occupation as physician assistant is from Wikipedia's candidate list.

name: Michael Guest
bio: Michael Guest has represented Mississippi's 3rd District since 2019 and chairs the House Ethics Committee. He sits on the Appropriations and Homeland Security committees, where he chairs the border security subcommittee. Before Congress he was a prosecutor for Madison and Rankin counties, serving as district attorney from 2008 to 2019.

platform.point: Chairs the Homeland Security subcommittee on border security and enforcement and supports a border wall.
Backs the 2017 tax cuts and lower corporate taxes to spur growth.
Member of the Pro-Life Caucus who sponsored a bill on infants who survive abortion.
Pledges to protect gun rights and voted against expanded background checks.
Chairs the House Ethics Committee and led the resolution to expel George Santos.

economy.evidence: Supported the 2017 tax cuts and argues lower corporate taxes promote growth.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: Pro-Life Caucus member; guns: voted against universal background checks in 2019 and 2021.

security.evidence: Former district attorney who opposed changing police accountability rules in 2021.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall and says undocumented immigrants must leave and re-enter.

foreign.evidence: Voted against the 2024 Ukraine aid package while supporting Israel after the 2023 Hamas attack.

energy.evidence: Voted against a 2020 bill assisting rural renewable electric energy.

tech.evidence: Voted against restoring net neutrality rules in 2019.

faith.evidence: Member of the Congressional Prayer Caucus.

notes: No campaign website could be confirmed.

name: Michael Chiaradio
bio: Michael Chiaradio is a regenerative farmer in Shubuta, Mississippi, and a former player in independent professional baseball. He grew up in New Jersey and moved to Mississippi in 2023. This is his first run for Congress.

platform.point: Wants lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs, more health workers and modern medical facilities.
Proposes favorable loans, debt relief and equipment rental programs for small farmers.
Favors moderate income taxes and a competitive corporate tax system with fewer loopholes.
Calls for federal investment in grid modernization and storm-hardened infrastructure.
Supports limiting stacked charges and using mental health alternatives.
Wants lower tariffs and more cooperation with China on trade.

economy.evidence: Proposes federal investment in industrial capital and moderate taxes, and opposes tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Calls for expanding low-cost access to health care and rental and mortgage assistance.

security.evidence: Criticized National Guard crime crackdowns and backs limits on stacked charges.

immigration.evidence: Describes managed immigration as an economic benefit while keeping border security.

foreign.evidence: Called Trump's meeting with Putin a sign of American decline.

notes: The campaign homepage image is a generated graphic rather than a headshot, so it was not recorded.

name: Erik Kiehle
bio: Erik Kiehle is a property management businessman from Meridian, Mississippi. He is a volunteer firefighter with two Lauderdale County departments and a private pilot.

platform.point: Describes himself as 'America First' and emphasizes national strength and security.
Pledges transparency and accountability to all constituents.
Promises to listen to local concerns and advocate for Mississippians.

notes: The campaign site states only general themes, so no positions were scored.

name: Mike Ezell
bio: Mike Ezell has represented Mississippi's 4th District since January 2023. He was Jackson County sheriff from 2014 to 2022. Before that he worked in law enforcement, including as a Pascagoula police captain and as Ocean Springs police chief.

platform.point: Prioritizes law enforcement support; sponsored a resolution condemning efforts to defund police.
Calls for stronger border security and immigration enforcement.
Supports more military spending and backs the Jones Act for domestic shipbuilding.
Wants spending cuts and a simpler tax code.
Supports fracking and says environmental regulations cost jobs.

economy.evidence: Favors cutting spending and simplifying the tax code and opposes higher taxes on the wealthy.

welfare.evidence: Opposes expanding the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only to save the mother's life, opposes same-sex marriage, strong gun rights, opposes vaccine requirements.

security.evidence: Supports qualified immunity and stricter punishment and opposes defunding police.

immigration.evidence: Opposes a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and calls for stronger border security.

foreign.evidence: Rejects avoiding foreign entanglements, calls China a threat and backs higher military spending.

energy.evidence: Supports fracking and opposes prioritizing green energy.

faith.evidence: Supports government partnerships with religious organizations.

notes: No campaign website with readable content could be confirmed.

name: Jeffrey Hulum III
bio: Jeffrey Hulum III has represented Gulfport in the Mississippi House's 119th District since winning a 2022 special election. He is a Gulfport native who retired as a sergeant major after 22 years in the U.S. Army. He founded Extend A Hand, Help A Friend, a nonprofit focused on food assistance.

platform.point: Aims to keep care and medicine affordable, address rural hospital closures and oppose health funding cuts.
Supports strong investment in public schools regardless of a child's ZIP code.
Wants living wages and policies that put working families ahead of corporate interests.
Seeks to balance community safety with fairness, accountability and rehabilitation.
Pledges to protect civil rights and voting access for all Mississippians.
Plans to tackle food insecurity on the Gulf Coast.

economy.evidence: Campaigns for living wages and putting working-class interests ahead of corporate wealth.

welfare.evidence: Says no family should go broke seeking care and opposes cuts to health funding.

education.evidence: Calls public school funding the best investment in future prosperity.

notes: New scores are based on general campaign-site statements rather than a voting record.

name: Carl Boyanton
bio: Carl Boyanton owns a produce store and is running as an independent from the Gulfport area. He ran for this seat as a Republican in 2020, 2022 and 2024. He describes himself as a principled conservative alternative to both major parties.

platform.point: Targets fraud, waste and improper payments and warns about the rising national debt and interest costs.
Supports congressional term limits to reduce the influence of career politicians.
Says life begins at conception and abortion should be banned except in rare circumstances.
Backs border security and reform that puts citizens and legal residents first.
Wants schools focused on core subjects rather than what he calls divisive ideologies.
Argues both major parties protect the status quo and shut out outside challengers.

economy.evidence: Focuses on cutting federal waste and reducing debt and spending.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: would prohibit it except in exceptional circumstances; no stated positions on other issues.

immigration.evidence: Calls for border security and immigration policy that prioritizes citizens and legal residents.

notes: The campaign image may be a graphic that includes his photo rather than a plain headshot.

name: Wesley Bell
bio: Wesley Bell has represented Missouri's 1st District since January 2025. He was St. Louis County prosecuting attorney from 2019 to 2025 and earlier served on the Ferguson City Council. He is a St. Louis County native who also worked as a municipal judge and prosecutor.

platform.point: Wants lower energy costs, action against grocery price gouging and caps on prescription drug prices.
Opposes Medicaid cuts and supports extending ACA subsidies.
Calls for defunding ICE and prosecuting agents who broke the law.
Supports writing abortion rights into federal law.
Promotes diversion programs and gun violence prevention measures.
Highlights federal funding for St. Louis infrastructure, housing and airport modernization.

economy.evidence: Supports cracking down on grocery price gouging and capping prescription drug prices.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Medicaid cuts and supports extending ACA subsidies.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: federal codification; LGBTQ: non-discrimination protections; guns: violence prevention measures; drugs: stopped low-level marijuana prosecutions.

security.evidence: Backs diversion programs and as prosecutor stopped prosecuting small marijuana possession cases.

immigration.evidence: Calls for defunding ICE and prosecuting agents who violated the law.

foreign.evidence: Voted in July 2026 against an amendment to cut off aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Supports clean energy jobs and environmental justice.

photo.author: Brian Thorpe, U.S. House of Representatives

name: Paul Berry III
bio: Paul Berry III is a St. Louis bail bondsman who has run for office several times. He won the 2026 Republican primary for Missouri's 1st District.

platform.point: Makes opposing socialist influence in St. Louis politics the center of his campaign.
Urges Republicans to unite behind Amendment 3 on the Missouri ballot.
Asks for statewide volunteers to phone bank and write letters in the 1st District.

economy.evidence: Campaigns against socialism and in favor of private enterprise.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: endorsed by Missouri Right to Life and urges support for Amendment 3; no other liberty issues are addressed.

notes: His campaign site uses the suffix III, while Wikipedia lists him as Paul Berry.

name: Tom Schmitz
current_role: Ward 4 vice chair, Libertarian Party of Missouri
bio: Tom Schmitz is the Ward 4 vice chair of the Libertarian Party of Missouri. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Libertarian primary for Missouri's 1st District.
notes: No campaign website or public issue statements were found.

name: Ann Wagner
bio: Ann Wagner has represented Missouri's 2nd District since 2013. She was U.S. ambassador to Luxembourg from 2005 to 2009, chaired the Missouri Republican Party from 1999 to 2005 and co-chaired the Republican National Committee. A St. Louis native, she held management positions at Hallmark Cards and Ralston Purina.

platform.point: Wants lower taxes and less regulation so workers keep more of their earnings.
Aims to address the national debt for future generations.
Supports energy independence through expanded domestic drilling and resource development.
Wants to use diplomatic alliances to strengthen national security and promote democracy.
Sponsored the SAVE Act targeting online advertising of trafficking victims.
Favors fewer federal mandates and more local control for teachers.

economy.evidence: Supports lower individual and corporate taxes, a flat tax and repeal of the estate tax.

welfare.evidence: Voted to keep welfare work requirements and for the 2017 ACA repeal bill.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: pro-life with a 20-week ban; guns: opposed universal background checks; LGBTQ: voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.

security.evidence: Voted for 2013 legislation to share cybersecurity data with the government.

immigration.evidence: Voted to bar DREAMers from military service and prioritizes border security.

foreign.evidence: Says diplomatic alliances should be used to advance national security and democracy.

energy.evidence: Signed the No Climate Tax Pledge and backs offshore drilling.

tech.evidence: Sponsored the SAVE Act penalizing online advertising of trafficking victims.

education.evidence: Has argued vouchers help low-income students leave low-performing schools.

faith.evidence: Supported a religious exemption from the ACA mandate and faith-based objections to same-sex marriage.
